project.title: Analysis of midgut composition of Lamypris noctiluca larvae
project.projectDescription: Firefly larvae are highly specialized predators of snails, which utilize midgut secretions to incapacitate and pre-digest their much larger prey.  With the current analysis we aim to shed light on the composition of the midgut secretion of these larvae utilizing a proteo-transcriptomic approach.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Two mass spectrometric analyses were performed, one with top-down and the other with bottom-up approach. In both cases midgut secretions of Lampyris noctiluca were first reduced with DTT and alkylated with CAA. For the bottom-up approach a digestion was performed with trypsin with an enzyme/substrate ratio of 1/75. The mass spectrometric analysis was then performed with a Q-Exactive Plus (Thermo Fisher Scientific) mass spectrometer coupled to an EASY nanoLC 1000 UPLC system 287 (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany).
project.dataProcessingProtocol: The software PEAKS 10 was used to match proteomic and transcriptomic data. PEAKS was run with a parent error mass tolerance of 10 ppm and 0.05 Da for fragment ions. As posttranslational modifications (PTMs), carbamidomethylation was set as fixed modification and acetylation (N-terminus, Lys), amidation, carboxylation (Glu), half of a disulfide bridge, carboxymethyl, oxidation (at Met, His, Trp) and pyroglutamate from Glu were accepted as variable modifications in the analysis. For enzymatically digested samples (bottom-up analyses), enzyme mode was set to ‘Trypsin’. For the sample without digestion (top-down analyses) ‘None’ was selected as enzyme mode.
